neighbours.label: the copula or '=' that links a unit to its measured value ("one day on Mars is ...", "1 euro = ...", "one mile is about ...")
fire: Most people are surprised that one year on Mercury is just 88 Earth days.
For travellers, 1 pound = 1.17 euros at today's rate.
Remember that one mile is about 1.6 kilometres when you read the map.
Oddly, a single day on Venus is longer than its whole year.
At the morning fixing, 1 dollar = 150 yen on the Tokyo market.
In practice one cup is roughly 240 millilitres in most recipes.
Astronomers note that one orbit of Neptune is about 165 Earth years.
On the converter page, 1 inch = 2.54 centimetres exactly.
quiet: Most people are surprised that the surface of Mercury is so heavily cratered.
For travellers, the pound is widely accepted in shops near the port.
Remember that the mountain trail is steep when you read the map.
Oddly, the atmosphere of Venus is thick, hot and full of acid clouds.
At the morning session, the dollar was steady on the Tokyo market.
In practice the measuring cup is kept in the top drawer.
Astronomers note that the planet Neptune is deep blue in colour.
On the converter page, the inch is listed under imperial units.

notes: In the probe, 'One day on Mars is' and '1 euro =' scored about 0.54 of max, 'is about 225' 0.29, 'comes to about' 0.22 and 'Mars is cold' 0.02. Near misses keep the same subjects with a non-quantity predicate.
